subtitle: The Last Echo of the Paramaras

panels.shot: wide, looming three-quarter view of Mandu fort on its plateau at dusk, with Alauddin Khalji's army encamped below and Mahalakadeva and Goga silhouetted on the ramparts
panels.action: Mahalakadeva and Goga stand side by side on the high walls of Mandu, cloaks pulled by the evening wind, as lines of tents and siege fires of the Delhi army stretch across the plain below the plateau.

dialogue.text: On 23 November 1305, as Mandu’s heights braced for assault, a broken kingdom, a minister called Goga, and a king named Mahalakadeva faced Alauddin Khalji’s general—and left one last voice in stone.

i18n.hi: २३ नवम्बर १३०५ को, हमले की आहट में थरथराता माण्डू, टूटा राज्य, गोगा नाम का वज़ीर और महालकदेव नाम का राजा, अलाउद्दीन खिलजी के सेनापति से भिड़े—और पत्थर में आख़िरी आवाज़ छोड़ गए।

panels.shot: slow push-in over a tattered royal parasol lying in dust beside a cracked temple wall at Dhar
panels.action: A fallen parasol bearing the faded emblem of the Paramaras lies in the dust near a weathered temple plinth, its cloth torn, while weeds creep through the cracks of once-fine stone.

dialogue.text: By the early fourteenth century, the Paramara kingdom of Malwa was a shadow of its age under Raja Bhoja. Dhar still held a throne, but its reach had shrunk and its rivals had grown.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी की शुरुआत तक, राजा भोज वाला परमार मालवा बस परछाईं रह गया था। धार में सिंहासन तो था, पर हदें सिकुड़ गई थीं, दुश्मन फलने लगे थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in Dhar court, slightly high angle, emphasizing the pressure on the throne and the prominence of Goga beside it
panels.action: In a modest yet dignified hall at Dhar, Mahalakadeva sits on a simple throne, face drawn but resolute, while Goga stands at his side with a commander’s straight back, scrolls and spears behind them.

dialogue.text: Mahalakadeva sat on Bhoja’s old throne, but command in the field had passed to his minister, Goga. Persian chroniclers would call him Koka and remember him as the real defender of Malwa.

i18n.hi: महालकदेव भोज के पुराने सिंहासन पर बैठते, पर मैदान की बागडोर अब उनके वज़ीर गोगा के हाथ में थी। फ़ारसी इतिहासों ने उसे ‘कोका’ लिखा, और असली रक्षक मालवा का वही ठहराया।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye view over central India with stylized arrows from Delhi towards Malwa, fading into a real landscape of marching troops
panels.action: A stylized view of the plains shows Delhi in the north, with a line of spearmen and pack-animals snaking south-west towards the Vindhyas, the image blending into a real column crossing dusty terrain.

dialogue.text: From Delhi, Alauddin Khalji turned his eye to Malwa. After Gujarat and Ranthambhor, he sent Ayn al-Mulk Multani to break this last independent corner, tighten his ring of power, and seize its wealth.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में बैठा अलाउद्दीन खिलजी की नज़र मालवा पर जा अटकी। गुजरात, रणथंभौर के बाद उसने अयन-उल-मुल्क मुल्तानी को भेजा—इस आख़िरी आज़ाद कोना तोड़ने, घेरा कसने, दौलत हथियाने।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of Ayn al-Mulk Multani’s vanguard cresting a ridge, but his face unseen, focusing on armor and banners
panels.action: Armoured horsemen crest a rocky rise, pennons streaming, their commander’s figure partly obscured, as infantry and archers press behind them toward wooded hills in the distance.

dialogue.text: Amir Khusrau, in his Khazain-ul-Futuh, sings of Multani’s march, claiming vast hosts and countless foes. His words are court praise, but they mark a real campaign of steel, calculation, and siege.

i18n.hi: अमीर खुसरो अपनी ‘ख़ज़ाइन-उल-फुतूह’ में मुल्तानी की चढ़ाई गाते हैं—बड़ी फ़ौजें, बेहिसाब दुश्मन। दरबारी तारीफ़ है, पर पीछे असली लोहा, चालाकी और घेरा-बंदी चल रही थी।

panels.shot: tight two-shot of Mahalakadeva and Goga in council, lamplight carving their faces, with a map of Malwa between them
panels.action: By the glow of oil lamps, Mahalakadeva and Goga bend over a rough map laid on a low table, showing Mandu, Dhar, Ujjain and Chanderi marked in ink, their faces tense yet controlled.

dialogue.speaker: Goga
dialogue.text: If we hold Mandu and break their first rush, Malwa still has breath.

i18n.hi: अगर माण्डू थाम लिया और उनकी पहली टक्कर तोड़ दी, तो मालवा में अभी जान बाकी है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mandu plateau seen from below, with defenders on ramparts and Goga riding along the walls
panels.action: Mandu’s high stone walls rise sheer from the cliffs, archers lining the battlements, while Goga rides along the inner rampart, gesturing orders to captains as Mahalakadeva watches from a tower balcony.

dialogue.text: Mandu became their shield. On that rugged plateau, Goga gathered what he could—the remnants of Paramara forces, hill-men, city guards—and braced for Multani’s onset.

i18n.hi: माण्डू उनकी ढाल बना। उस खुरदरे पठार पर गोगा ने जो मिला, इकट्ठा किया—परमार के बचे सिपाही, पहाड़ी लोग, शहर के पहरेदार—और मुल्तानी की टक्कर को तैयार खड़ा हो गया।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-range battle scene outside Mandu, focusing on Goga’s contingent clashing with advancing Delhi cavalry
panels.action: On uneven ground below Mandu, lines of Malwa footmen brace with spears as Delhi horsemen close in; dust rises in sheets, and a standard bearing a lion emblem sways amidst the clash.

dialogue.text: Amir Khusrau describes fierce fighting before Mandu. He praises Multani’s charge and tells of Goga’s resistance, of lines breaking and reforming in the dust and cries at the foot of the hill.

i18n.hi: अमीर खुसरो माण्डू के नीचे भयंकर लड़ाई लिखते हैं। वे मुल्तानी की टक्कर की वाहवाही करते हैं और गोगा की जद्दोजहद—टूटती, फिर जुड़ती पंक्तियाँ, धूल और नारे, पहाड़ी की गोद में—का ज़िक्र करते हैं।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Goga captured, hands bound, kneeling; Mahalakadeva glimpsed far away on the walls as a tiny figure
panels.action: In a trampled field, Goga kneels with his hands bound, face unbowed, ringed by Delhi soldiers; distant on Mandu’s heights, a tiny figure of Mahalakadeva is barely visible against the sky.

dialogue.text: In the struggle outside, Goga fell into the hands of Multani’s men. Court chroniclers do not dwell on his words at capture. They dwell on what his fate was made to say.

i18n.hi: बाहर की टक्कर में गोगा मुल्तानी के सिपाहियों के हाथ चढ़ गया। दरबारी लेख उसकी गिरफ़्तारी की बात नहीं खींचते, वे ज़्यादा उसके अंजाम से दिया गया संदेश लिखते हैं।

panels.shot: grim close-up of a covered bundle on a cart leaving the battlefield, soldiers around; camera angle from behind, destination unseen
panels.action: A rough cart rolls away from the battlefield, guarded by mail-clad riders; on it lies a long, wrapped shape, carefully lashed, while the evening light throws long shadows ahead.

dialogue.text: Amir Khusrau records that Goga’s head was severed and sent to Delhi. In the panegyric, it becomes a trophy of obedience and terror, a warning carried across the plains to Alauddin’s court.

i18n.hi: अमीर खुसरो लिखते हैं कि गोगा का सिर काटकर दिल्ली भेजा गया। उनकी तारीफ़-नामा में वह सिर आज्ञा और दहशत की निशानी बन जाता है—मैदानों पर लहराती चेतावनी, अलाउद्दीन के दरबार तक।

panels.shot: wide shot inside a lofty hall in Delhi, low angle on Alauddin’s throne with a distant tray presented below, faces of courtiers half-lit
panels.action: In a grand hall with high pillars, courtiers stand in careful ranks as a covered metal tray is presented at the base of a raised throne; the seated sultan’s figure is distant, observing in cool silence.

dialogue.text: In Delhi, the arrival of Goga’s head was made spectacle. Chroniclers describe it to magnify Alauddin’s might and the fall of Malwa’s minister, a courtly ritual of victory and humiliation.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में गोगा के सिर की आमद तमाशा बना दी गई। इतिहासकार उसे ऐसे लिखते हैं कि अलाउद्दीन की हैसियत और मालवा के वज़ीर का पतन दोनों और ऊँचे दिखें—दरबारी फ़तह और बेइज़्ज़ती का मेले जैसा रस्म।

panels.shot: majestic mid-shot of the Dhar iron pillar standing in a courtyard, viewed slightly from below to emphasize its height and antiquity
panels.action: A tall iron pillar rises in a courtyard at Dhar, its surface dark and smooth with age, flanked by old stone-work and quiet trees, as a few townsfolk gaze up at it in the morning light.

dialogue.text: With Goga gone, Multani moved on Dhar, the Paramara capital. Amir Khusrau notes the breaking of the great iron pillar there—an ancient emblem of the dynasty’s endurance and pride.

i18n.hi: गोगा के हटते ही मुल्तानी धार की ओर बढ़ा, परमारों की राजधानी। अमीर खुसरो वहाँ के उस बड़े लोहे के स्तम्भ के गिराए जाने का ज़िक्र करते हैं—पुरानी निसान जिसकी पकड़ में वंश की जान और शान थी।

panels.shot: dynamic close shot of Delhi soldiers heaving ropes around the iron pillar, the moment before it cracks, faces strained
panels.action: Armoured soldiers strain on ropes looped about the iron pillar as wedges bite at its base; the metal is beginning to tilt, while onlookers in the background watch with a mix of awe and dread.

dialogue.text: Khusrau boasts how the Dhar pillar was cast down. His verse presents it as the fall of Paramara strength itself, a sign that their line, once towering, now lay toppled in the dust.

i18n.hi: खुसरो फूले नहीं समाते कि धार का स्तम्भ धराशायी हुआ। उनकी कविता में वह खुद परमार ताक़त की गिरावट है—जो कभी ऊँचा उठता खड़ा था, अब धूल में चित पड़ा निशान।

panels.shot: sunset wide shot of Mandu fort again, this time ringed by siege works, towers and trenches, tents closer and more numerous
panels.action: Mandu’s walls stand silhouetted against a burning sunset, now tightly ringed by siege towers, trenches and rows of tents; smoke from campfires coils upward around the plateau.

dialogue.text: Yet Mandu still held. As Multani’s men tightened the siege, Mandu’s cliffs and walls turned days into weeks of stalemate. The question now was not attack—but entry.

i18n.hi: पर माण्डू अब भी टिका रहा। मुल्तानी की फ़ौज घेरा कसती गई, तो माण्डू की चट्टानें और दीवारें दिनों को हफ़्तों की बराबरी में खींच लाईं। अब मसला धावे का नहीं था—घुसने का था।

panels.shot: tense interior shot in a dim Mandu passageway, with a shadowed figure leading Delhi soldiers toward a narrow gate from inside
panels.action: Inside a narrow, dimly lit passage cut into the rock, a cloaked local guide moves ahead, glancing back, as Delhi soldiers creep behind him, their armor dull in the torchlight, toward a low exit.

dialogue.text: Sources speak of betrayal—a secret entrance shown to the besiegers. On 23 November 1305, Multani’s men slipped through a hidden way, turning Mandu’s height from shield into trap.

i18n.hi: किताबें ख़यानत की बात करती हैं—घेराबंदियों को किसी ने छुपा रास्ता दिखा दिया। २३ नवम्बर १३०५ को मुल्तानी के लोग गुप्त राह से भीतर सरक गए—और माण्डू की ऊँचाई ढाल से फाँस बन गई।

panels.shot: urgent medium shot of Mahalakadeva inside Mandu, armor hastily donned, as news of the breach reaches him
panels.action: In an inner courtyard, Mahalakadeva stands with hastily donned armor, a messenger pointing toward the inner gate; his face is pale but steady as the sound of distant struggle drifts in.

dialogue.speaker: Mahalakadeva and Goga
dialogue.text: If the walls fail, we stand by the springs that fed our fathers.

i18n.hi: अगर दीवारें टूट जाएँ, तो हम उन चश्मों के पास डटेंगे, जिनसे हमारे पुरखे प्यास बुझाते थे।

panels.shot: somber wide shot near a rocky spring within Mandu, with Mahalakadeva’s small force facing advancing Delhi troops among rocks and trees
panels.action: Among rocks and scrub beside a clear spring inside Mandu, Mahalakadeva’s small band forms a rough line with shields raised, as Delhi soldiers advance between boulders, weapons held ready.

dialogue.text: Tradition in the chronicles says Mahalakadeva was killed near a spring. There, in that last stand within his own fortress, the direct line of Paramara kings ended in close-pressed combat.

i18n.hi: इतिहास की परम्परा कहती है, महालकदेव एक चश्मे के पास मारे गए। अपने ही क़िले के दिल में, उस आख़िरी मोर्चे पर, परमार राजाओं की सीधी रेखा हाथापाई में ख़त्म हो गई।

panels.shot: quiet aftermath shot inside Mandu: abandoned weapons and a deserted courtyard, smoke haze softening the scene
panels.action: A silent Mandu courtyard lies strewn with discarded shields and spears; a thin haze of smoke hangs in the air, and a single banner of the Paramaras has fallen, half-covering a stone step.

dialogue.text: After Mandu’s fall, Malwa passed under Delhi’s control. Amir Khusrau exults in the conquest, swelling numbers and victories, but behind his verses lie emptied courtyards and silenced councils.

i18n.hi: माण्डू के गिरते ही मालवा दिल्ली के ताबे में चला गया। अमीर खुसरो फ़तह पर झूमते हैं, गिनतियाँ और जीतें बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर लिखते हैं, पर उन पंक्तियों के पीछे सूने आँगन हैं, खामोश दरबार।

panels.shot: transition shot from a carved Paramara emblem fading into Alauddin-era administrative figures distributing orders over Malwa
panels.action: A carving of a Paramara emblem on stone slowly fades into the image of officials seated with scrolls and account-books, overseeing scribes and messengers in a Malwa town under new authority.

dialogue.text: Within years, Delhi’s governors and tax-collectors settled into Malwa’s cities. Castles, markets, and temples that once answered to Dhar now answered to the Khalji sultanate’s officers.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही सालों में दिल्ली के सूबेदार और वसूलदार मालवा के नगरों में जम गए। किले, बाज़ार और मंदिर, जो कल तक धार के कहने पर चलते थे, अब खिलजी सल्तनत के अफ़सरों को जवाब देने लगे।

panels.shot: serene close-up of the 1310 Udaipur inscription on a stone slab, sunlight grazing the carved letters, surroundings slightly blurred
panels.action: Sunlight grazes the carved letters of a stone inscription at Udaipur in Madhya Pradesh, the grooves catching shadow, while the rest of the shrine courtyard around it lies softly out of focus.

dialogue.text: Yet in 1310, a stone at Udaipur in Madhya Pradesh still bore a Paramara grant. H.V. Trivedi published its text—a faint, final assertion of authority carved five years after Mandu’s capture.

i18n.hi: फिर भी १३१० में, मध्यप्रदेश के उदयपुर की एक शिला पर अब भी परमारों की एक दान-पट्टा उकेरी थी। एच.वी. तिवेदी ने उसका लेख छापा—माण्डू गिरने के पाँच साल बाद, पत्थर पर गढ़ी हल्की, आख़िरी हुक्मरानी।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Mandu’s ruins at sunrise, with distant figures of modern visitors walking among them
panels.action: At sunrise, the ruins of Mandu’s walls and palaces glow softly, birds circling overhead, while a few modern visitors walk along the ramparts, small against the vast sky and stone.

dialogue.text: Mahalakadeva, Goga, Ayn al-Mulk, and Alauddin are gone; their choices remain in forts, broken pillars, and one last inscription. A dynasty ended, but its history still speaks, if we listen to the stone.

i18n.hi: महालकदेव, गोगा, अयन-उल-मुल्क और अलाउद्दीन सब मिट गए; उनकी चोइसें आज भी किलों में, टूटे स्तम्भों में, और एक आख़िरी अभिलेख में पड़ी हैं। वंश खत्म हुआ, पर उसका किस्सा अब भी बोलता है—जो पत्थर की सुन सके।

subtitle_i18n.en: The Last Echo of the Paramaras
